message.content:
Below is a concise overview of the key rights and protections you have as a tenant in Texas. (This is general information and not legal advice; for specific situations you may want to consult an attorney or a local tenant‑rights organization.) | Area | What the law says | Practical Tips | |------|-------------------|----------------| | **Security Deposit** | • Landlords may charge up to one month’s rent for a furnished unit and two months for an unfurnished unit.
• The deposit must be returned within 30 days after you move out, minus any lawful deductions (e.g., unpaid rent, damage beyond normal wear). | • Get a written receipt and keep a copy of the lease.
• Take photos or videos of the unit before moving in and after moving out. | | **Habitability** | • Texas law requires landlords to maintain the premises in a safe, sanitary, and livable condition.
• Repairs for health and safety issues (plumbing, heating, electrical, structural) must be made promptly. | • Report problems in writing (email or text) and keep a record.
• If the landlord fails to act, you may withhold rent or repair and deduct, but do so only after following the proper procedure. | | **Rent Payment** | • Rent is due on the date specified in the lease.
• Late fees are allowed only if the lease states them and they are reasonable. | • Keep a copy of the lease and any payment receipts. | | **Entry Rights** | • Landlords must give at least 24 hours written notice before entering, except in emergencies.
• Entry is allowed for repairs, inspections, or showing the unit to prospective tenants or buyers. | • Ask for a written notice and keep a copy. | | **Discrimination** | • Under the Texas Fair Housing Act and federal law, landlords cannot discriminate based on race, color, religion, sex, national origin, disability, familial status, or other protected classes. | • If you suspect discrimination, file a complaint with the Texas Commission on Human Rights or the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development. | | **Lease Termination** | • Either party may terminate a month‑to‑month lease with 30 days’ written notice.
• For fixed‑term leases, the landlord must provide a valid reason for early termination (e.g., non‑payment, violation of lease). | • Review your lease for any specific termination clauses. | | **Eviction Process** | • Landlords must follow the Texas eviction procedure: serve a written notice (e.g., 3‑day notice for non‑payment), file a lawsuit, and obtain a court order.
• Eviction cannot be carried out without a court order. | • Respond promptly to notices.
• If you receive an eviction notice, consider contacting a tenant‑rights group or attorney. | | **Repair and Deduct** | • If the landlord fails to repair a major problem, you may repair it yourself and deduct the cost from rent, but you must follow the proper steps (notice, attempt to get landlord to fix, keep receipts). | • Document all communications and keep receipts. | | **Right to Quiet Enjoyment** | • You have the right to live in the unit without unreasonable interference from the landlord or other tenants. | • Report any harassment or disturbances to the landlord in writing. | | **Privacy** | • Landlords cannot enter the unit without notice, except in emergencies. | • Keep a log of any entries. | | **Utilities** | • The lease should specify who pays utilities. | • Verify utility responsibilities before signing. | | **Subletting** | • Subletting is allowed only if the lease permits it or the landlord consents. | • Get written permission before subletting. | | **Maintenance of Common Areas** | • Landlords must keep common areas clean and safe. | • Report any hazards in common areas. | ### Resources | Resource | What it offers | |----------|----------------| | **Texas Attorney General – Consumer Protection Division** | Information on landlord‑tenant laws, dispute resolution, and consumer rights. | | **Texas Commission on Human Rights** | File discrimination complaints. | | **Local Tenant‑Rights Organizations** | Free or low‑cost legal assistance, workshops, and advocacy. | | **Legal Aid of North Texas / Texas Legal Services** | Free legal help for qualifying tenants. | | **U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD)** | National fair housing resources and complaint filing. | --- #### Quick Checklist Before Signing a Lease 1. **Read the lease thoroughly** – look for clauses on rent, security deposit, maintenance, entry, and termination. 2. **Ask for a written receipt** of the security deposit. 3. **Document the unit’s condition** with photos or a video walkthrough. 4. **Confirm who pays utilities** and any other recurring costs. 5. **Verify that the landlord has a valid license** (if required) and that the property meets local building codes. If you have a specific issue (e.g., a landlord refusing to make repairs, a dispute over a security deposit, or a potential eviction notice), let me know and I can provide more targeted guidance or help you draft a letter to your landlord.
